newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks end mixed after directionless session.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks end mixed after directionless session.

text.p: Tokyo stocks ended mixed in directionless trade on Wednesday with the key Nikkei edging up slightly. After an initial dip at the open on Wall Street's losses, buying was limited to selected blue-chip issues, while the recent fall in other issues lost momentum, brokers said.
The key Nikkei 225 average inched up 29.35 points or 0.14 percent to finish at 20,659.91. But its December futures closed 10 points lower at 20,650.
"No fresh money seemed to flow into the market, and I expect the downside to become vulnerable," said Masaaki Higashida, strategist at Nomura Securities Co Ltd.
"Only a limited number of major issues was bought, and it was not encouraging market sentiment at all," Higashida said.
Declining issues outnumbered advancing ones 638 to 422, while 183 issues were unchanged on the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange (TSE).
Turnover was a modest 277 million shares on Wednesday, confirming the day's lacklustre trade. On Tuesday, it was 269 million shares.
In other indices, the broader TOPIX index ended marginally higher, gaining 0.72 points or 0.05 percent to 1,536.36.
The Nikkei 300 average ended up 0.45 points or 0.16 percent to 290.59.
A total of 283 issues slid to their year lows on the first section on Wednesday, the largest daily total for this year, surpassing Tuesday's 274 issues.

Seiki Orimi, an analyst at Dai-Ichi Securities Co Ltd, said that the Nikkei 225 average had entered a consolidation phase, and that the directionless trade might continue at least until the middle of December.
He also said overseas fund managers seemed to have aggressively dumped underperforming issues.
"But that selling (by foreign investors) has ceased for now," Orimi said.
Among sectors, losers were led by air transport, sea transport, pulp/paper, land transport and brokerages.
The major gaining sectors were communications, precision instruments, automobiles, fisheries and miscellaneous manufacturers.
Shares in the air transport sector were weaker on a dim earnings outlook for many firms.
Japan Airlines Co Ltd (JAL) dropped to a low for this year.
JAL's shares fell to as low as 632 yen, below its previous low, marked on October 31, of 650 yen. It ended eight yen lower at 644 yen.
Shares in All Nippon Airways Co Ltd lost 24 yen to end at 926 yen, after briefly falling to 925 yen, their lowest level for this year.
Meanwhile, selective buying in blue-chip companies headed towards Sony Corp shares, which closed 160 yen higher at 7,430 yen. It was Sony's highest level for this year.
The second section index dropped 9.69 points or 0.50 percent to close at 1,931.42. Volume was 10.77 million shares.
The over-the-counter (OTC) index was down 5.55 points to stand at 1,367.83 as of 0718 GMT.
-- Hiroko Nakata, Tokyo Equities Desk +81-3-3432-8027
